accepted_records.title: CERN Technical & Doctoral Studentship
accepted_records.eligibility_summary: National of a CERN Member or Associate Member State; enrolled (or about to start) a doctoral programme; university must agree the research contributes to the doctoral thesis; good command of English or French.
accepted_records.benefits_summary: Tax-free monthly subsistence allowance of CHF 3,907, comprehensive health insurance (CHIS), family supplements (CHF 531/mo with spouse, CHF 1,062/mo with children), travel to Geneva, 30 days paid annual leave.
accepted_records.target_audience: Doctoral students in applied physics, engineering, computing, data science, mathematics
accepted_records.discovered_via: Nexora legacy database enrichment (official site verification)
accepted_records.short_original_summary: Research placement at CERN in Geneva where doctoral students contribute directly to their thesis while working on accelerator and physics projects.
accepted_records.verification_notes: Verified on official careers.cern programme page. Applications reopen August 6, 2026; call dates vary through the year. 2026-cycle deadline not yet published.
accepted_records.duration: Initial 6 months, renewable up to 3 years
application_steps: Submit online application via the CERN careers portal when the call opens
Attach CV and university enrolment details
Confirm thesis agreement with home university
accepted_records.apply_cta_notes: Opens the CERN careers doctoral studentship page.
accepted_records.time_needed_to_apply: A few hours (online form plus CV)
accepted_records.official_deadline_note: Applications for the next batch reopen August 6, 2026; exact call deadline TBC.
before_you_apply_checklist: Confirm your nationality is a CERN Member/Associate Member State
Ensure your university supports thesis research at CERN
accepted_records.why_this_is_trustworthy: Verified directly on the official CERN careers portal.
accepted_records.recommendation_reason: World-class research environment with a strong tax-free stipend and health coverage.
accepted_records.who_should_apply: Doctoral students in physics, engineering, computing or mathematics at CERN member-state universities.
accepted_records.who_should_not_apply: Students from non-member states, or those whose home university cannot support thesis research at CERN.
prep_tips: Start your thesis agreement conversation early
Prepare a focused CV highlighting lab or computing experience

accepted_records.title: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026
accepted_records.eligibility_summary: PhD held at the call deadline; maximum 8 years of full-time research experience post-PhD (exclusions apply); mobility rule — no more than 12 months in the host country in the 36 months before the deadline.
accepted_records.benefits_summary: Living allowance (gross, country-corrected, typically €4,000–€8,000+/mo), €710/mo mobility allowance, €660/mo family allowance, plus research, training, networking and management unit costs.
accepted_records.discovered_via: Nexora legacy database enrichment (official site verification)
accepted_records.short_original_summary: Europe's flagship postdoctoral fellowship funding international mobility and intersectoral research with generous allowances and research costs.
accepted_records.verification_notes: Verified on official European Commission MSCA pages. Call HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01-01 deadline September 9, 2026, 17:00 CEST. Budget €399.05M, ~1,600 projects expected.
accepted_records.host_institution: Any eligible host organisation in EU/Associated Countries
application_steps: Find a host organisation and supervisor
Write the proposal with the host
Submit via the EU Funding & Tenders portal
accepted_records.apply_cta_notes: Opens the EU Funding & Tenders topic page for MSCA-PF-2026.
accepted_records.time_needed_to_apply: Several weeks to months (proposal, host agreement)
accepted_records.official_deadline_note: Single-stage call closes September 9, 2026 at 17:00 CEST.
before_you_apply_checklist: Secure a host institution and supervisor
Check the 8-year experience and 12-month mobility rules
accepted_records.why_this_is_trustworthy: Verified on the official European Commission MSCA call documentation.
missing_or_unclear_info: Country correction coefficient for your host country
accepted_records.recommendation_reason: The most prestigious EU postdoctoral fellowship with strong funding and career mobility.
accepted_records.who_should_apply: Postdocs with up to 8 years of post-PhD experience seeking international mobility in Europe.
accepted_records.who_should_not_apply: Researchers over the 8-year experience cap or failing the mobility rule.
prep_tips: Start the proposal early — it is the deciding factor

accepted_records.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship for Postdoctoral Researchers
accepted_records.eligibility_summary: Completed doctorate within the last 4 years (extensions for documented career breaks); all nationalities and disciplines; no more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying; no prior Humboldt fellowship.
accepted_records.benefits_summary: Monthly fellowship of €3,000, subsidies for health and liability insurance, mobility lump sum, family allowances for accompanying spouse/children, intensive German language course.
accepted_records.target_audience: Postdoctoral researchers of all nationalities and disciplines
accepted_records.discovered_via: Nexora legacy database enrichment (official site verification)
accepted_records.short_original_summary: Prestigious fellowship funding postdocs to carry out independent research in cooperation with a host institution in Germany.
accepted_records.verification_notes: Verified on official humboldt-foundation.de. Three calls per year (800-application cap per call); next call opens November 15, 2026 for a July 2027 selection.
accepted_records.host_institution: German research institution of your choice
application_steps: Select a host researcher at a German institution
Obtain the host's mentoring agreement
Apply online via the Humboldt portal during an open call
accepted_records.apply_cta_notes: Opens the Humboldt Foundation application portal (registration required).
accepted_records.time_needed_to_apply: Several weeks (host agreement, CV, research outline)
accepted_records.official_deadline_note: Next call opens November 15, 2026; selection in July 2027.
before_you_apply_checklist: Confirm doctorate is within the last 4 years
Secure a host and mentoring agreement
accepted_records.why_this_is_trustworthy: Verified directly on the official Alexander von Humboldt Foundation site.
missing_or_unclear_info: Exact call close date (portal closes when the 800-application cap is reached)
accepted_records.recommendation_reason: One of Germany's most prestigious postdoctoral fellowships, open to all nationalities and disciplines.
accepted_records.who_should_apply: Postdocs within 4 years of their doctorate seeking long-term research in Germany.
accepted_records.who_should_not_apply: Those who have exceeded the Germany stay limits or already hold a Humboldt fellowship.

accepted_records.title: United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP) 2026
accepted_records.eligibility_summary: Age 32 or under in the year of the exam; nationality of a participating UN Member State; first-level university degree (Bachelor's); fluency in English or French. A second language (the other of English/French or an official UN language) is required for many posts.
accepted_records.benefits_summary: Entry into the UN Professional category (P-2/P-3) with an international civil service salary, benefits and allowances package, career development pathway, and opportunities for global rotations within the UN system.
accepted_records.target_audience: Early-career professionals (Bachelor's+), 32 or younger, from UN Member States
accepted_records.discovered_via: Nexora legacy database enrichment (official UN Careers site verification)
accepted_records.short_original_summary: The UN's flagship competitive examination that recruits early-career professionals from Member States into entry-level international civil service positions across the UN system.
accepted_records.verification_notes: Verified on the official UN Careers YPP page. The 2026 exam cycle applications have closed; the programme recurs annually with participating Member States and age/nationality rules published per cycle.
application_steps: Check participating Member States and confirm your nationality and age eligibility
Create an account on the UN Careers portal
Submit the online application during the open window
If shortlisted, take the written YPP examination
Attend the interview if you pass the exam
accepted_records.apply_cta_notes: Opens the official UN Careers YPP page with cycle dates and application instructions.
accepted_records.time_needed_to_apply: A few hours (online form) plus exam preparation
accepted_records.official_deadline_note: The 2026 application window has closed; the next annual cycle and its exact dates are announced on the official page.
before_you_apply_checklist: Confirm your country is a participating UN Member State
Verify you are 32 or under in the exam year
Check the second-language requirement for your target posts
accepted_records.why_this_is_trustworthy: Verified directly on the official UN Careers website.
accepted_records.recommendation_reason: The most direct route into a UN career for early-career professionals from participating Member States.
accepted_records.who_should_apply: University graduates aged 32 or under from UN Member States seeking an international civil service career.
accepted_records.who_should_not_apply: Candidates over 32, nationals of non-participating states, or those without a first-level degree.

Confirm language requirements per post before applying

accepted_records.title: Horizon Europe Frontier Science Research Grant
accepted_records.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since their PhD and scientific independence; host institution must be in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Career breaks can extend the eligibility window.
accepted_records.benefits_summary: Up to €1.5 million over 5 years (extendable to €2 million for starting grants with additional costs); 100% of eligible direct costs plus 25% indirect cost contribution. Covers staff, equipment, travel and research expenses.
accepted_records.target_audience: Early-career research leaders (PhD + 2-7 years) across all disciplines
accepted_records.discovered_via: Nexora legacy database enrichment (official ERC/EU portal verification)
accepted_records.short_original_summary: Horizon Europe's flagship frontier-science funding stream, delivered through the European Research Council, supports excellent investigator-driven research in any field across Europe.
accepted_records.verification_notes: Verified on the official ERC and EU Funding & Tenders portal. Frontier science under Horizon Europe is funded through the ERC grant schemes; the ERC-2027-STG (Starting Grant) call closes October 14, 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time.
accepted_records.host_institution: Public or private research institution in EU/Associated Country
required_documents: Research proposal (B1+B2) following the ERC template
application_steps: Identify a host institution in the EU or an Associated Country
Prepare the research proposal (B1) and extended proposal (B2)
Submit via the EU Funding & Tenders portal before the call deadline
accepted_records.apply_cta_notes: Opens the ERC-2027-STG call page on the EU Funding & Tenders portal.
accepted_records.official_deadline_note: ERC-2027-STG closes October 14, 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time.
before_you_apply_checklist: Confirm your host institution is eligible
Check the PhD + 2-7 year eligibility window (extensions for career breaks)
Start the proposal early — peer review is rigorous
accepted_records.why_this_is_trustworthy: Verified on the official European Research Council funding pages.
missing_or_unclear_info: Exact budget envelope for the 2027 call (published on the portal)
accepted_records.recommendation_reason: Europe's most prestigious frontier-research grant, open to excellent early-career PIs in any discipline.
accepted_records.who_should_apply: Early-career principal investigators with 2-7 years post-PhD experience seeking substantial independent research funding.
accepted_records.who_should_not_apply: Researchers outside the eligibility window or without a host institution in an eligible country.
prep_tips: Align your proposal with ERC evaluation criteria (excellence only)
Secure host-institution commitment before the deadline
